k: An alien ooze from a meteorite
st: A symbiote rides a meteorite to Central Park, bonds with Peter, then Eddie Brock, and dies with Eddie in a pumpkin bomb blast.

k: Alien lifeforms that need a host to survive
Knull's creations, who locked him away
st: A Life Foundation probe brings four symbiotes from a comet; they need human hosts, and only Venom survives.
Kasady swallows a piece of Venom and spawns Carnage, which Venom devours, but a piece of Carnage lives on in Mulligan.
Venom and Eddie are pulled into another universe, then sent home, leaving a small piece of the symbiote behind.
Freed by Venom, Imperium's captive symbiotes bond with its staff against Knull's Xenophages, and Venom dies to destroy the Codex.

k: Knull's hunters, sent for the Codex
st: Knull sends Xenophages to Earth for the Codex, until Venom draws them into acid and Strickland's grenades destroy them.
In season 1, ice creatures from Pluto freeze the city and take Dr. Smartyr, hoping he can help them get home.

k: Hairy, ape-like people who live underground
st: In season 2, the Molemen sink banks into their underground city and plot an invasion, until Spider-Man captures the Mole.

k: A tribe of primitive blue giants
st: In season 2, in 3,000,000 B.C., Spider-Man wins the blue giants' stone city back from radium-mutated plant monsters.
In season 3, blue giants in another dimension tell Spider-Man their world is too cold, and he defeats the plants chilling it.

k: Plant monsters that live on radium
st: In season 2, radium-mutated plant monsters rule the blue giants' city, until Spider-Man takes their radium gems and they wither.
In season 3, another society of intelligent plants chills the giants' world, until Spider-Man takes their radium and they wither.

k: Tiny aliens from the planet Gorth
st: In season 3, Infinata destroys Gorth, and its last scientist dies on Earth after giving Spider-Man the planet's knowledge.
In season 3, Dr. Atlantean sinks Manhattan under a dome to help the Atlanteans invade, until Spider-Man webs him up.

k: An alien ooze from an asteroid
st: In season 1, a symbiote rides John Jameson's shuttle to Earth, bonds with Peter, then Eddie Brock, and is shot into space.
In season 3, Dormammu brings it back to Eddie, it spawns Carnage, and Venom drags Carnage through a portal.
In season 2, Morbius becomes a plasma-craving vampire and tries to turn everyone into one, as Blade hunts him.
In season 4, Blade learns his mother is Miriam, the Vampire Queen, who wants the Neogenic Recombinator to make more vampires.
In season 5, Black Cat, Morbius and Blade battle Miriam and her vampires.

k: Animal-human hybrids of the High Evolutionary
st: On Counter-Earth, the High Evolutionary's animal-human Bestials rule over humans and hunt the human rebels.

k: Alien symbiotes that bond with hosts
st: Venom and Carnage reach Counter-Earth, serve the Synoptic, and millions of symbiotes are unleashed on the planet.

k: An alien that rode a shuttle to Earth
st: In season 1, a symbiote rides John Jameson's shuttle home and bonds with Peter, then Eddie Brock, who becomes Venom.
In season 2, Eddie bonds with it again, its spores infect John Jameson, and Spider-Man separates it from Eddie for good.
A symbiote comes through Norman's gateway; Strange and Peter force it back through, but a piece is left behind for Norman.

k: People born with powers from a genetic mutation
st: Mutants come out of hiding to stop Shaw's nuclear war, and the US and Soviet fleets fire on them.
Feared by humans, mutants face a Registration Act, and Magneto tries to mutate world leaders by force.
William Stryker raids Xavier's school and uses Cerebro to try to kill every mutant alive, until the X-Men stop him.
A cure for the mutant gene splits mutants, and Magneto's army storms Alcatraz to destroy its source.
In 2023, Sentinels have nearly wiped out mutants, until Logan's trip to 1973 changes history and saves them.
No mutants have been born in 25 years, and Logan gets a group of lab-made mutant children to the Canadian border.

k: Shape-shifting aliens who lost their world
st: The cosmic force in Jean wiped out the D'Bari world, and Vuk's survivors take human forms on Earth to claim it.
Jean disintegrates the D'Bari attacking the mutants' train, then kills Vuk in space.
In season 1, Sentinels hunt mutants, the Morlocks hide underground, and the X-Men free Genosha's mutant slaves.
In season 4, Magneto offers every mutant a haven on Asteroid M, until Fabian Cortez seizes it and Magneto destroys it.
In season 5, Magneto readies a mutant army on Genosha, then stands down when Gyrich nearly kills Xavier.
In season 1, Genosha joins the UN as a mutant nation, until Sentinels massacre it and Prime Sentinels attack mutants worldwide.
In season 2, the US bans the X-Men, so Xavier bases them on Genosha as X-Corp, where they stop Apocalypse.

k: Aliens of a distant solar system
st: In season 3, Dark Phoenix consumes a star, and the Shi'ar declare she destroyed the D'Bari solar system.

k: Aliens of a vast star empire
st: In season 3, the Shi'ar fight over the M'Kraan Crystal as D'Ken tries to remake the universe, then put Dark Phoenix on trial.
In season 5, Lilandra takes the dying Xavier to the Shi'ar homeworld to be healed.
In season 1, the Shi'ar fight the Kree as Lilandra plans to wed Xavier, and Deathbird challenges him.
In season 1, Ronan's Kree battle Deathbird and the Shi'ar Imperial Guard in a war between the two empires.

k: Humanoid insects that spread by spores
st: In season 3, the Colony crash on Earth and infect people with spores, then leave Earth with Rogue's first love, Cody.
In season 2, the Brood overrun a Weapon X lab and infect Wolverine, until the lab explodes and destroys them.
In season 5, the Phalanx try to assimilate all life on Earth, until Warlock spreads Beast's virus and destroys them.
In season 2, Mojo pulls the X-Men into his dimension to die on his shows, until Longshot forces their return.
In season 3, Longshot, leader of a rebellion against Mojo, escapes to Earth, then goes home to finish the fight.
In season 1, Mojo traps Jubilee and Roberto inside a deadly video game made for his viewers.

k: Blood drinkers who rule from the shadows
st: Pure-blood elders rule the vampires in secret, until the turned vampire Deacon Frost seizes power to wake La Magra.
A Reaper plague tears through Prague's vampires, until Blade and the Bloodpack wipe out the Reapers.
Vampires revive Drake, the first vampire, but the Daystar virus made with his blood kills the vampires around him.
In Detroit, Marcus Van Sciver of the House of Chthon builds a virus to kill pureblood vampires and unleashes it.

k: Mutant vampires that feed on vampires
st: A plague spreads from Jared Nomak, turning vampires into Reapers who feed on vampires and humans alike.
Blade's UV bomb wipes out the Reaper nest, and Nomak, the first Reaper, dies by Blade's sword.
On Attilan, their hidden city on the Moon, Maximus seizes the throne and drives the Royal Family to Hawaii.
As Attilan fails, Black Bolt leads his people to Earth through Eldrac, and the city is destroyed.

k: Aliens who live on by taking human bodies
st: In season 2, Karolina learns Jonah's alien family is buried in a ship under Los Angeles, and they come to possess Pride members.
Nico's staff makes Jonah's family vanish, and Xavin takes Jonah's newborn daughter, Elle, into space.
